finalists.label: Pontine Facial Nerve Palsy
finalists.why: Strong evidence from lesion location and electrophysiological tests supports this diagnosis.

finalists.label: Facial nerve palsy
finalists.why: Clinical presentation of facial muscle weakness and specific signs like disappearance of nasolabial fold support this diagnosis.

frontier_selector.why: The lesion located in the dorsolateral right pons and significantly decreased amplitude of the right facial nerve compound muscular action potential compared to the healthy side decisively support Pontine Facial Nerve Palsy over the more general Facial nerve palsy.

support_spans: Lesion located in dorsolateral right pons
Significantly decreased amplitude of right facial nerve compound muscular action potential compared to healthy side
Presence of insertional activity in right facial muscles with greatly reduced voluntary activity
contradict_spans: No vertebrobasilar artery main trunk occlusion or stenosis
